A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on SAM, memorization, and membership privacy. All 20 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial restructuring and a changed title.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, membership-inference, optimizer, and defense experiments on four benchmark datasets, alongside synthetic and entropy-bucket analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original experiments on five benchmark datasets, direct SAM memorization and influence analyses, and Hessian-trace measurements, alongside retained empirical results.

M1.justification: Sharp in v3 Equation (5) matches the simplified SharpReg objective already given in v2 Appendix C.4.1, Equation (17), with beta = lambda/(1 + lambda - xi). SAM and the influence-entropy construction remain substantively unchanged. Computing SAM-specific scores applies existing definitions rather than introducing a new optimization procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds EyePacs diabetic-retinopathy classification and membership evaluation, extending medical coverage from hospital records to retinal images. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Purchase-100, and Texas-100 remain. The synthetic typical/atypical classification example is retained in Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: SWA disappears from the entropy-bucket performance comparison, and the evaluated AdvReg, MemGuard, and SELENA defense comparisons are removed. Correctness-based and multi-query attack comparisons also disappear, while four probability-based attacks remain. Sharp is the renamed SharpReg objective, not an additional comparator.

E3.justification: v3 Equation (4) defines equally weighted member/nonmember accuracy, replacing the pooled accuracy stated in v2 Appendix C.3; this establishes a reported metric revision, not necessarily reruns. New analyses introduce influence filtering above 0.2 and top-20 selection within memorization intervals. EyePacs adds balanced-batch training, and the reported CIFAR-10 Sharp setting changes from equivalent beta 0.625 to 0.6818.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct SAM-versus-SGD memorization distributions, influence regressions, tiger case analysis, bucket-overlap analysis, and Hessian-trace validation of Sharp. It removes v2's sharpness and regularization sweeps, early-stopping tradeoff analysis, and SharpReg bucket-performance analysis. The synthetic example and architecture comparison are retained rather than new supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 reports means and standard deviations over five randomized attack-data splits. v3 retains the five-run mean statement but removes standard deviations from its results table, without restoring uncertainty estimates in the appendices. This removes the paper's reported dispersion estimates; it does not establish a reduction in run count.

E6.justification: v3 adds EyePacs results, including test accuracies of 75.41% for SAM and 73.67% for SGD, and Hessian traces of 1556.54, 307.87, and 84.18 for Sharp, SGD, and SAM. It adds SAM-score findings, revises bucket-performance curves and parts of the attack tables, and removes defense and multi-query results. Many appendix values are retained; changed metrics and reporting conventions preclude treating revised scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 Section 5 and Appendix C introduce a majority/minority/noise mixture model, minority-subclass alignment ordering, a threshold attacker, two theorems, and four lemmas with proofs and explicit assumptions. v2 has no corresponding theoretical development. The influence-entropy formula and simplified sharpness objective were already present.

C1.justification: v3 retains the claims connecting SAM's atypical-sample generalization and membership risk, but adds computing/releasing SAM scores and a theoretical explanation as headline contributions. It removes mitigation strategies as a principal contribution and centers the paper on explaining the apparent generalization/privacy contradiction.

C2.justification: v3 develops the atypical-pattern hypothesis into specific interpretations about redistributed memorization, increased influence of moderately memorized samples, and image-versus-tabular privacy differences. It replaces v2's largely data-dependent interpretation of scores with optimizer-specific analysis. Discussions of early stopping, excessive-regularization failure, limited gains on typical data, and the entropy metric's computational impracticality are removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds EyePacs preprocessing, model, and training details and lists per-dataset Sharp parameters. It removes v2's tuning grids and explicit first-order implementation description, while retaining most existing training schedules and source/code references. The claimed SAM-score release has no new access location specified, and EyePacs batch size is inconsistent: 100 versus 12 samples from each of five classes.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work around generalization versus membership privacy and connects its theoretical setup to Chen et al. (2023), Kou et al. (2023), and newer SAM/noise research including Baek et al. (2024). Much of the defense and label-only survey, plus the Andriushchenko et al. counterpoint, is removed. The foundational Feldman and SAM positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statement, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Privacy experiments precede the memorization analysis, the toy example moves to an appendix, and the mitigation section is replaced by theory. The title, author block, terminology, and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds memorization/influence panels and a Hessian table, redraws bucket plots, and replaces the entropy histogram with an SGD/SAM density comparison. The attack table moves forward and changes column structure and highlighting; defense displays and multi-query columns disappear. The original toy figure and influential-image montage are retained as v3 Figures 5 and 3.

improvement.justification: Direct SAM-score analyses address v2's reliance on SGD-derived scores, while EyePacs, Hessian checks, and conditional theory strengthen the explanatory evidence. However, v3 removes uncertainty estimates and multi-query results showing lower SAM vulnerability on CIFAR. It also changes the attack metric and reports five-run means while retaining many values previously described as single-run results, without reconciliation. These substantive gains and reporting losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
